# Motive MCP connector

Let your AI read your Motive fleet: where every truck and driver is, Hours of Service clocks and violations, inspection reports, safety events, fault codes, IFTA mileage and fuel purchases. The AnythingMCP connector gives Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Cursor and Gemini 22 MCP tools for Motive, all read-only.

[![Open Motive in AnythingMCP Cloud](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open%20in-AnythingMCP%20Cloud-1f6feb?style=for-the-badge)](https://cloud.anythingmcp.com/login?mode=register&redirect=%2Fconnectors%2Fstore%3Finstall%3Dmotive&utm_source=github&utm_medium=catalog&utm_campaign=motive)

## Start without code

No installation and no terminal: AnythingMCP Cloud runs the Motive connector for you, operated by helpcode.ai in Frankfurt, Germany.

1. **Click the button above** and create an account or sign in. The Motive connector opens, ready to install.
2. **Paste the API key or token from your Motive account.** Every click is in the [step-by-step guide](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/motive-to-mcp).
3. **Click Install.** AnythingMCP shows the address of your MCP server.
4. **Add that address to your assistant:** [Claude](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-motive-to-claude) · [ChatGPT](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-motive-to-chatgpt) · [Microsoft Copilot](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-motive-to-copilot) · [Cursor](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-motive-to-cursor) · [Gemini CLI](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-motive-to-gemini) · [Meta Muse](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-motive-to-muse).
5. **Ask your first question.**

Prefer help with the setup? [Talk to us](https://anythingmcp.com/contact).

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  client["Claude · ChatGPT · Copilot · Cursor"]
  amcp["AnythingMCP<br/>roles · audit log · encrypted credentials"]
  api["Motive API<br/>api.gomotive.com"]
  client -- "MCP, OAuth or API key" --> amcp
  amcp -- "HTTPS, an API key" --> api
```

- **The AI client** speaks MCP (Streamable HTTP) to AnythingMCP and only sees tool names, descriptions and results. It never gets the Motive credentials.
- **AnythingMCP** checks the client's role, builds the call from the tool definition, adds the credentials (an API key), calls Motive, logs the call and returns the result.
- **Motive** sees an ordinary API client with the rights of the account the credentials belong to.

## Tool reference

Every parameter as the AI client sees it in `tools/list`. Source: [`packages/backend/src/adapters/intl/motive.json`](../../../packages/backend/src/adapters/intl/motive.json).

### `motive_list_vehicles`

List the company vehicles in Motive: id, number (the fleet unit name), status, VIN, make, model, year, license plate, fuel type, IFTA flag, groups, the ELD device and the current or permanent driver. Use it to find a vehicle id for the location, inspection, fault code and IFTA tools. Read-only, paginated.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /v1/vehicles`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `driver_ids` | integer[] | no | Only vehicles linked to these driver (user) ids. |
| `fuel_type` | `diesel` \| `gasoline` \| `propane` \| `lng` \| `cng` \| `ethanol` \| `methanol` \| `e85` \| `m85` \| `a55` \| `biodiesel` \| `other` | no | Only vehicles with this fuel type. |
| `updated_after` | string | no | Only records changed after this moment (ISO 8601, for example 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z). Useful for incremental syncs. |
| `per_page` | integer | no | Records per page (default 25, at most 100). |
| `page_no` | integer | no | Page number, starting at 1. The answer carries pagination.total; ask for the next page while page_no * per_page is below it. |
| `time_zone` | string | no | Optional time zone for the timestamps in the answer, sent as X-Time-Zone (for example "Eastern Time (US & Canada)" or "America/New_York"). Without it the company time zone applies. |
| `metric_units` | boolean | no | Optional, sent as X-Metric-Units: true returns kilometres, litres and metric units, false miles and gallons. Without it the company setting applies. |

### `motive_get_vehicle`

Read one vehicle by its Motive id: number, status, VIN, make, model, year, plate, fuel type, groups, ELD device and assigned driver. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /v1/vehicles/{vehicle_id}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle_id` | integer | yes | Motive vehicle id (the numeric id from motive_list_vehicles, not the unit number). |
| `time_zone` | string | no | Optional time zone for the timestamps in the answer, sent as X-Time-Zone (for example "Eastern Time (US & Canada)" or "America/New_York"). Without it the company time zone applies. |
| `metric_units` | boolean | no | Optional, sent as X-Metric-Units: true returns kilometres, litres and metric units, false miles and gallons. Without it the company setting applies. |

### `motive_lookup_vehicle`

Find a vehicle by its fleet unit number (the "number" shown in the Motive dashboard, for example "Truck 12") and return its full record including the Motive id. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /v1/vehicles/lookup`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `number` | string | yes | Vehicle number exactly as set in Motive. |
| `time_zone` | string | no | Optional time zone for the timestamps in the answer, sent as X-Time-Zone (for example "Eastern Time (US & Canada)" or "America/New_York"). Without it the company time zone applies. |
| `metric_units` | boolean | no | Optional, sent as X-Metric-Units: true returns kilometres, litres and metric units, false miles and gallons. Without it the company setting applies. |

### `motive_list_vehicle_locations`

Current location of every vehicle (v2): for each vehicle its id, number, VIN and current_location with latitude, longitude, a place description, located_at, bearing, speed, odometer, engine hours, fuel level and the current driver. Use it for "where is truck X" or a fleet map. Works for all ELD types. Read-only, paginated.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /v2/vehicle_locations`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle_ids` | integer[] | no | Only these vehicle ids. |
| `vehicle_status` | `active` \| `deactivated` | no | Only active or only deactivated vehicles. |
| `per_page` | integer | no | Records per page (default 25, at most 100). |
| `page_no` | integer | no | Page number, starting at 1. The answer carries pagination.total; ask for the next page while page_no * per_page is below it. |
| `time_zone` | string | no | Optional time zone for the timestamps in the answer, sent as X-Time-Zone (for example "Eastern Time (US & Canada)" or "America/New_York"). Without it the company time zone applies. |
| `metric_units` | boolean | no | Optional, sent as X-Metric-Units: true returns kilometres, litres and metric units, false miles and gallons. Without it the company setting applies. |

### `motive_list_vehicle_gateway_locations`

Current location of vehicles fitted with the Motive Vehicle Gateway (v3), with richer telemetry than v2 and, on request, the auxiliary (PTO) status. For vehicles on older ELDs use motive_list_vehicle_locations. Read-only, paginated.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /v3/vehicle_locations`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle_ids` | integer[] | no | Only these vehicle ids. |
| `vehicle_status` | `active` \| `deactivated` | no | Only active or only deactivated vehicles. |
| `include_aux_details` | boolean | no | Include the auxiliary input status of each vehicle (default false). |
| `per_page` | integer | no | Records per page (default 25, at most 100). |
| `page_no` | integer | no | Page number, starting at 1. The answer carries pagination.total; ask for the next page while page_no * per_page is below it. |
| `time_zone` | string | no | Optional time zone for the timestamps in the answer, sent as X-Time-Zone (for example "Eastern Time (US & Canada)" or "America/New_York"). Without it the company time zone applies. |
| `metric_units` | boolean | no | Optional, sent as X-Metric-Units: true returns kilometres, litres and metric units, false miles and gallons. Without it the company setting applies. |

### `motive_get_vehicle_location_history`

Location breadcrumbs of one vehicle between two dates (v2): each point with latitude, longitude, description, located_at, speed, bearing, odometer, engine hours and driver. The range may span at most 3 months; keep it short for a readable answer. Read-only.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /v2/vehicle_locations/{vehicle_id}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle_id` | integer | yes | Motive vehicle id from motive_list_vehicles. |
| `start_date` | string | yes | First day of the history (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `end_date` | string | yes | Last day of the history, at most 3 months after start_date (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `updated_after` | string | no | Only records changed after this moment (ISO 8601, for example 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z). Useful for incremental syncs. |
| `time_zone` | string | no | Optional time zone for the timestamps in the answer, sent as X-Time-Zone (for example "Eastern Time (US & Canada)" or "America/New_York"). Without it the company time zone applies. |
| `metric_units` | boolean | no | Optional, sent as X-Metric-Units: true returns kilometres, litres and metric units, false miles and gallons. Without it the company setting applies. |

### `motive_list_driver_locations`

Drivers with their last known location and the vehicle they are in: user id, name, current_location (lat, lon, description, located_at) and current_vehicle. Read-only, paginated.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /v1/driver_locations`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| `metric_units` | boolean | no | Optional, sent as X-Metric-Units: true returns kilometres, litres and metric units, false miles and gallons. Without it the company setting applies. |

### `motive_list_users`

List the users of the Motive account (drivers, fleet users and admins): id, first and last name, email, phone, role, status, duty status, driver company id, licence details and time zone. Filter by role=driver to get the driver list. Read-only, paginated.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /v1/users`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `role` | `driver` \| `fleet_user` \| `admin` | no | Only users with this role. |
| `duty_status` | `off_duty` \| `on_duty` \| `sleeper` \| `driving` \| `waiting` | no | Only drivers currently in this duty status. |
| `status` | `active` \| `deactivated` | no | Only active or only deactivated users. |
| `name` | string | no | Search by first name, last name or both. |
| `updated_after` | string | no | Only records changed after this moment (ISO 8601, for example 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z). Useful for incremental syncs. |
| `per_page` | integer | no | Records per page (default 25, at most 100). |
| `page_no` | integer | no | Page number, starting at 1. The answer carries pagination.total; ask for the next page while page_no * per_page is below it. |
| `time_zone` | string | no | Optional time zone for the timestamps in the answer, sent as X-Time-Zone (for example "Eastern Time (US & Canada)" or "America/New_York"). Without it the company time zone applies. |
| `metric_units` | boolean | no | Optional, sent as X-Metric-Units: true returns kilometres, litres and metric units, false miles and gallons. Without it the company setting applies. |

### `motive_list_available_time`

Hours of Service clocks per driver: current duty status and the time still available on the drive, shift, cycle and break clocks (in seconds), plus the recap of on-duty time per day. Use it to answer "who can still drive today and for how long". Read-only, paginated.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /v1/available_time`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `driver_ids` | integer[] | no | Only these driver (user) ids. |
| `per_page` | integer | no | Records per page (default 25, at most 100). |
| `page_no` | integer | no | Page number, starting at 1. The answer carries pagination.total; ask for the next page while page_no * per_page is below it. |
| `time_zone` | string | no | Optional time zone for the timestamps in the answer, sent as X-Time-Zone (for example "Eastern Time (US & Canada)" or "America/New_York"). Without it the company time zone applies. |
| `metric_units` | boolean | no | Optional, sent as X-Metric-Units: true returns kilometres, litres and metric units, false miles and gallons. Without it the company setting applies. |

| `status` | string | no | Only logs in this status, as Motive reports it on each log. |
| `updated_after` | string | no | Only records changed after this moment (ISO 8601, for example 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z). Useful for incremental syncs. |
| `per_page` | integer | no | Records per page (default 25, at most 100). |
| `page_no` | integer | no | Page number, starting at 1. The answer carries pagination.total; ask for the next page while page_no * per_page is below it. |
| `time_zone` | string | no | Optional time zone for the timestamps in the answer, sent as X-Time-Zone (for example "Eastern Time (US & Canada)" or "America/New_York"). Without it the company time zone applies. |
| `metric_units` | boolean | no | Optional, sent as X-Metric-Units: true returns kilometres, litres and metric units, false miles and gallons. Without it the company setting applies. |

### `motive_list_inspection_reports`

Driver vehicle inspection reports (DVIRs, v2) for vehicles and trailers: date, driver, vehicle or asset, inspection type, location, odometer, defects with their category, notes and resolution status, and signatures. Filter status=with_defects to find open problems. Read-only, paginated.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /v2/inspection_reports`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `driver_ids` | integer[] | no | Only reports by these driver (user) ids. |
| `vehicle_ids` | integer[] | no | Only reports for these vehicle ids. |
| `asset_ids` | integer[] | no | Only reports for these asset (trailer) ids. |
| `start_date` | string | no | First report day (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `end_date` | string | no | Last report day (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `status` | string | no | all, with_defects, with_no_defects or with_signature_missing; with defect-level resolution also open, acceptable or resolved, otherwise satisfactory, harmless or corrected. |
| `entity_type` | string | no | vehicle for truck reports or asset for trailer reports. |
| `updated_after` | string | no | Only records changed after this moment (ISO 8601, for example 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z). Useful for incremental syncs. |
| `per_page` | integer | no | Records per page (default 25, at most 100). |
| `page_no` | integer | no | Page number, starting at 1. The answer carries pagination.total; ask for the next page while page_no * per_page is below it. |
| `time_zone` | string | no | Optional time zone for the timestamps in the answer, sent as X-Time-Zone (for example "Eastern Time (US & Canada)" or "America/New_York"). Without it the company time zone applies. |
| `metric_units` | boolean | no | Optional, sent as X-Metric-Units: true returns kilometres, litres and metric units, false miles and gallons. Without it the company setting applies. |

### `motive_list_driver_performance_events`

Safety events detected by Motive (v2): harsh acceleration, braking and cornering, crashes, and with AI dashcams events such as cell phone use, seat belt, tailgating, stop sign violations and drowsiness. Each event has type, time, location, speed, driver, vehicle, coaching status and media links when recorded. Defaults to the last week. Read-only, paginated.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /v2/driver_performance_events`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `driver_ids` | integer[] | no | Only events of these driver (user) ids. |
| `vehicle_ids` | integer[] | no | Only events in these vehicle ids. |
| `event_types` | string[] | no | Only these event types, for example hard_brake, hard_accel, hard_corner, crash, seat_belt_violation, tailgating, cell_phone, stop_sign_violation, distraction, unsafe_lane_change, drowsiness, forward_collision_warning, near_miss, smoking. |
| `start_date` | string | no | First day (default one week ago) (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `end_date` | string | no | Last day (default today) (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `updated_after` | string | no | Only records changed after this moment (ISO 8601, for example 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z). Useful for incremental syncs. |
| `media_required` | boolean | no | true: only events with a video or image attached. |
| `ignore_thresholds` | boolean | no | true: return every event, also those below the configured severity thresholds. |
| `per_page` | integer | no | Records per page (default 25, at most 100). |
| `page_no` | integer | no | Page number, starting at 1. The answer carries pagination.total; ask for the next page while page_no * per_page is below it. |

### `motive_list_fault_codes`

Engine fault codes (diagnostic trouble codes) reported by the vehicles: code, label, description, source, status (open or closed), type, first and last observed time and the vehicle. Defaults to the last 7 days. Read-only, paginated.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /v1/fault_codes`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle_ids` | integer[] | no | Only codes from these vehicle ids. |
| `status` | `open` \| `closed` | no | Only open or only closed codes. |
| `type` | `constant` \| `intermittent` | no | Only constant or only intermittent codes. |
| `start_date` | string | no | First day (default 7 days ago) (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `end_date` | string | no | Last day (default today) (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `updated_after` | string | no | Only records changed after this moment (ISO 8601, for example 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z). Useful for incremental syncs. |
| `per_page` | integer | no | Records per page (default 25, at most 100). |
| `page_no` | integer | no | Page number, starting at 1. The answer carries pagination.total; ask for the next page while page_no * per_page is below it. |
| `time_zone` | string | no | Optional time zone for the timestamps in the answer, sent as X-Time-Zone (for example "Eastern Time (US & Canada)" or "America/New_York"). Without it the company time zone applies. |
| `metric_units` | boolean | no | Optional, sent as X-Metric-Units: true returns kilometres, litres and metric units, false miles and gallons. Without it the company setting applies. |

### `motive_list_driving_periods`

Driving periods of the vehicles: each stretch of driving with start and end time, duration, distance, origin and destination, vehicle and driver, and type (driving, PC for personal conveyance, YM for yard move). Filter assigned_to_driver=false for unidentified driving. Defaults to the last 7 days. Read-only, paginated.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /v1/driving_periods`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `driver_ids` | integer[] | no | Only periods of these driver (user) ids. |
| `vehicle_ids` | integer[] | no | Only periods of these vehicle ids. |
| `type` | `driving` \| `PC` \| `YM` | no | driving, PC (personal conveyance) or YM (yard move). |
| `status` | `in_progress` \| `complete` \| `interrupted` | no | Only periods in this state. |
| `assigned_to_driver` | boolean | no | true: only periods with a driver; false: only unidentified driving. |
| `start_date` | string | no | First day (default 7 days ago) (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `end_date` | string | no | Last day (default today) (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `updated_after` | string | no | Only records changed after this moment (ISO 8601, for example 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z). Useful for incremental syncs. |
| `per_page` | integer | no | Records per page (default 25, at most 100). |
| `page_no` | integer | no | Page number, starting at 1. The answer carries pagination.total; ask for the next page while page_no * per_page is below it. |
| `time_zone` | string | no | Optional time zone for the timestamps in the answer, sent as X-Time-Zone (for example "Eastern Time (US & Canada)" or "America/New_York"). Without it the company time zone applies. |

### `motive_list_assets`

List the non-powered assets (trailers, containers, equipment): id, name, type, status, make, model, year, VIN, plate, groups and the asset gateway. Read-only, paginated.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /v1/assets`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | no | Search by asset name. |
| `exact_match` | boolean | no | true: name must match exactly, including case (default false). |
| `status` | `active` \| `deactivated` | no | Only active or only deactivated assets. |
| `per_page` | integer | no | Records per page (default 25, at most 100). |
| `page_no` | integer | no | Page number, starting at 1. The answer carries pagination.total; ask for the next page while page_no * per_page is below it. |
| `time_zone` | string | no | Optional time zone for the timestamps in the answer, sent as X-Time-Zone (for example "Eastern Time (US & Canada)" or "America/New_York"). Without it the company time zone applies. |
| `metric_units` | boolean | no | Optional, sent as X-Metric-Units: true returns kilometres, litres and metric units, false miles and gallons. Without it the company setting applies. |

### `motive_list_asset_locations`

Last known location of the assets that carry a Motive asset gateway: asset id and name, latitude, longitude, place description, located_at and battery state. Read-only, paginated.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /v1/asset_locations`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | no | Only the asset with this name. |
| `per_page` | integer | no | Records per page (default 25, at most 100). |
| `page_no` | integer | no | Page number, starting at 1. The answer carries pagination.total; ask for the next page while page_no * per_page is below it. |

### `motive_list_groups`

List the groups of the account (the way the fleet is split into terminals, regions or teams): id, name, parent group, status and member counts. Use a group to understand which vehicles and drivers belong together. Read-only, paginated.

## Run it yourself

AnythingMCP is open source (AGPL-3.0). [Run it with Docker](../../../README.md#run-it-yourself), open **Connectors → Store**, pick **Motive** and enter `MOTIVE_API_KEY`, then add your MCP server URL to the AI client.
